devotions.titel: The Life Jesus Came to Give
devotions.citaat: I believe that God intends for every one of us to live a life of fulfillment. To live life to the full. To live wholeheartedly.

zinnen.tekst: On Sunday the speaker opened with this: God intends for every one of you to live a life of fulfillment. Full of life, full of freedom, full of peace, full of love.
He knows this isn't everybody's reality, but he believes it's God's design, and that it's possible for every one of us to live this way.
One of the keys he finds in Numbers 14, where God says of Caleb: he has a different spirit and follows me wholeheartedly.
That's the title of the message: Following God wholeheartedly. And the subtitle: living in the fullness of forgiveness, free from the pain of the past.
God wants you to live wholeheartedly: to put your whole heart into your life, without constantly protecting your heart or checking yourself.
A life with an internal freedom and peace, full of faith, hope and love. It's the life that Jesus came to give us. How good is that?
There are things that can and do stop us from living wholeheartedly, and one of them is unforgiveness: not dealing with pain.
Later in the message he says: God loves you. God's for you. He doesn't want this to be a theory, he wants it to be your reality.
What would it look like to follow Him with your whole heart today?

gebed.tekst: Lord, search my heart. Holy Spirit, bring to mind what I can handle, whatever is stopping me from wholeheartedly following You.

devotions.titel: Fully Seen, Fully Known, Fully Loved
devotions.citaat: You are fully seen, fully known, fully loved. I'm not talking about your opinions or your actions, but who you really are. Not only does he love you, he delights in you.

zinnen.tekst: The key to living wholeheartedly, the speaker says, is founded in how you see God.
Right back in the garden, the enemy came to get people to question God: Did God really say that? Does God really love you? Is God really for you?
Those are the questions of the enemy, and he wants to keep you from the fullness of life.
Jesus said it as clearly as it gets, in John 10:10: the enemy comes to steal, kill and destroy, but I have come that you might have life, and life to the full.
The Father has qualified you. You don't need to qualify. He has rescued you from the dominion of darkness and brought you into the kingdom of the Son he loves.

He told about a cabin in the middle of nowhere, where dark is dark and he had to feel his way around. That's the dominion of darkness: you can't see the truth about God, and you can't see the truth about yourself.
In that dark we try to work our lives out, and we try to determine our value by our performance or by how other people see us.
Do you realize it? You are fully seen, fully known, fully loved. Not only does He love you, He delights in you. So good.
How do you see Him today, and do you believe He delights in you?

gebed.tekst: Lord, I release it to You, knowing that I am safe in Your hands. There's no safer place in this world than in Your hands.

devotions.titel: Forgive As the Lord Forgave You
devotions.citaat: We forgive because we've already been forgiven. We receive grace and we give that grace. We are loved and we give that love. God starts this.

zinnen.tekst: God has forgiven our sins in Christ. Colossians tells us, the speaker says, that we have redemption, we have the forgiveness of sins.
Sometimes shame and pain stop us from coming to God with our whole heart. But Hebrews 4:16 says you can boldly come to the throne of grace and find help in your time of need.
Being forgiven and extending forgiveness belong together, he says. Colossians 3:13: forgive as the Lord forgave you.
He doesn't just want to talk about forgiveness. He wants to minister forgiveness, so that you live in its fullness.
Because the price of unforgiveness is just too high. You may be wounded once, but unforgiveness makes you relive it a thousand times.
It keeps you tied to the person who hurt you, in your own heart. They live in your heart rent free.
What happened to you may not be your fault, but what you do with it is your responsibility.
You don't choose the wound, but you do choose what you do with the wound. And that's where forgiveness comes in.
Where could you give the grace you've received from Him today?

gebed.tekst: God, I'm going to trust You with this. I surrender to You because I trust You, even if I don't fully understand. I know You're good, I know You're for me, and I release it into Your hands.

devotions.citaat: Forgiveness will free you. Unforgiveness will imprison you.

zinnen.tekst: When you hold on to a debt, you think you're making them pay, but you're the one paying the price. The longer you hold on to offense, the more the offense holds on to you.
But here's the thing: you can trust Jesus with the justice.
Jesus told Peter to keep forgiving, and then he told him why: a king cancels a servant's debt that was way beyond what he would earn in a lifetime.

The speaker believes Jesus is showing us how life works: we were designed to live in love, grace and mercy, and when we refuse to live that way after receiving forgiveness from God, something happens inside us.
Hurt people hurt people, until someone breaks the cycle with forgiveness. And you are called to be one of those people.
Forgiveness isn't saying that what they did is okay. It isn't forgetting, it isn't reconciliation, and it doesn't mean denying justice.
It means: I acknowledge what happened, I acknowledge that it hurt, but I choose not to carry that debt anymore. I release it into God's hands because I trust God with it.
You forgive not because they deserve freedom. You forgive because you deserve freedom. Come on.
Is there a debt you could put into His hands today, trusting Him with the justice?

gebed.tekst: Search me, God. What do I need to trust You with? Where am I holding unforgiveness?

devotions.citaat: When you bring it into the light, God doesn't shame you. But it's in his light that we will find healing.

zinnen.tekst: Sometimes the pain is so great that we hide it in some storage cupboard in our heart. But hiding it doesn't mean it's healed. It keeps it in the darkness, and that darkness is what you've been rescued from.
So he encourages you: whatever it is for you, bring it to God honestly.
God wants you to live with an inner freedom, and to live the life you were created for.
Jesus opened the scroll in the temple and read: the Spirit of the Lord is on me, he has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners and to set the oppressed free.

The speaker has had things to deal with himself. For years he has prayed for himself and his wife to have children, and they haven't seen a miracle there. Then the question comes: can I really trust God with everything?
He worked through that by knowing God's nature and character. Sometimes we see a part, He sees fully. God's picture is eternal, and you can wholeheartedly trust Him.
He has had to work through deep betrayals from people close to him, but he chooses to live with a freedom of heart. And he wants you to live wholeheartedly in all that God's got for you.

With David in Psalm 139 he reads: search me, God, know my heart, lead me in your way. He doesn't believe the Holy Spirit will bring up more than you can handle today. It's one step at a time. God loves you. God's for you.
What would you like to bring into His light today?

gebed.tekst: Lord, show me what's stopping me from living free from the pain, so that my past won't hold me captive to my future. Holy Spirit, I release it to You.

devotions.citaat: Anything that would separate us from God, Jesus took upon himself on the cross, that we could have a right relationship with our loving Father in heaven.

zinnen.tekst: At the end of the message the speaker spoke to anyone who doesn't have a relationship with God: I'm talking about how good God is, and how Jesus has come to bring that.
In Jesus you are rescued from the dominion of darkness and brought into the kingdom of his Son. You have redemption, forgiveness of sins, freedom, and fullness of life.
And it's not just for this lifetime. The most significant part of your life is eternal, and Jesus came to restore you to a right relationship with God.
You can feel your way around in the spiritual darkness of this lifetime and somehow make it work, like he did in that dark room. But you can't do that for eternity.
He is here to tell you: God sees you, God loves you, God's for you. And Jesus paid a high price for you to live in the fullness of all that God created you for.
He asked: if that's you, raise your hand. And he said: I believe this is the best decision you can make in your life.
Then the whole church family prayed together: I thank you that my past will not determine my future, but my relationship with you will.
And you don't have to do life alone, or your journey with God alone. The church isn't perfect, but they're for you, and they're not going to hold your past against you.
What will you thank Jesus for today, for what He has done for you?

gebed.tekst: Dear Jesus, thank You for what You've done for me. I accept that You died for me, for the forgiveness of my sins, and that You rose again to give me this new life. I choose to live Your way and step into the fullness of life that You died to give me.

slot.tekst: Unforgiveness costs you far more than it costs the person who hurt you. Forgiveness is not letting them off; it is how you get your own heart back.
